blocks.intro_md:
There are many guides to electronic resources for Jewish scholarship, such as that of university library guides, as well as other websites. However, many of these guides are meant for students and researchers, and less for the general educated reader with an interest in these topics. In addition, many previous guides are from ten years ago or longer, and many of the links no longer work.

Here are some guides that I found especially useful:

notes_md: See [here](http://www.jewishdigitalcollections.com/jewish-studies-guides.html) for “a list of guides prepared by university librarians worldwide to help students taking courses in Jewish studies” by Diane Romm, published no later than 2018. See [the About page](http://www.jewishdigitalcollections.com/about.html). Thanks to A. Berman for pointing out this guide. Unfortunately many of the links are now broken. For a relevant university syllabus, see [Prof. Aaron Ahrend’s syllabus to his course “Research Guidance in Bibliography and Writing”](https://talmud.biu.ac.il/sites/talmud/files/shared/%D7%AA%D7%9C%D7%9E%D7%95%D7%93%20%D7%A1%D7%99%D7%9C%D7%91%D7%95%D7%A1%D7%99%D7%9D%20%D7%AA%D7%A9%D7%A4%D7%91/%D7%90%D7%A8%D7%A0%D7%9309101%D7%94%D7%93%D7%A8%D7%9B%D7%94.pdf). I took this course many years ago as part of my MA in Talmud at Bar-Ilan. The course and course packet went over many digital tools, however the syllabus available online only gives topic headings, and bibliography of published articles.
